lead: Emergency drill stations on a mannequin with a team: PPH, eclampsia, shoulder dystocia, cord prolapse and newborn resuscitation. The first words in every drill are "call for help".
f: Help, note the time · ABC, O₂ 15 L/min · 2 large cannulae, bloods, cross-match 4–6 units, warm fluids · rub up the uterus · find the 4 Ts (tone, trauma, tissue, thrombin) · catheter

sc: Soft uterus, heavy bleeding after birth → Rub up the uterus and give oxytocin

f: Oxytocin 10 IU slow IV, then 40 IU in 500 mL over 4 h · ergometrine 0.5 mg IM (not in hypertension or heart disease) · misoprostol 800 µg sublingual · carboprost 250 µg deep IM every 15 min, max 8 (not in asthma) · tranexamic acid 1 g IV within 3 h · bimanual compression, balloon, theatre

Help · left lateral, airway, O₂ · MgSO₄ 4 g IV over 5–15 min (8 mL of 50% diluted to 20 mL) → 1 g/h for 24 h · recurrent fit: 2 g · control BP (labetalol, hydralazine) · fluids ≤ 80 mL/h · deliver once stable · no pump: 4 g IV + 10 g IM (5 g each buttock), then 5 g IM 4-hourly

sc: Fit at 36 wk, BP 170/112 → Eclampsia: MgSO₄ 4 g IV

f: Before each dose: knee jerk present, RR ≥ 12, urine ≥ 30 mL/h · order of signs: lost reflexes → respiratory depression → arrest · antidote calcium gluconate 10 mL of 10% IV over 10 min

sc: Reflexes absent, RR 16 → Stop MgSO₄, check level

f: Help · evaluate episiotomy · legs (McRoberts) · suprapubic pressure from the baby's back (80% delivered) · enter (Rubin II, Woods screw) · remove the posterior arm · roll onto all fours · record each manoeuvre, its time and who did it · no fundal pressure
Push the presenting part up, keep it up · knee-chest or exaggerated left Sims · fill the bladder with 500 mL · terbutaline 0.25 mg SC · Category 1 CS (instrumental if fully dilated)

Dry, warm, assess tone, breathing, heart rate · airway in neutral position · 5 inflation breaths, then ventilate · HR < 60 after 30 s of good ventilation → compressions 3 : 1 · Apgar at 1, 5 min (then every 5 min if < 7)
